metadata.pending_cut_realization:
Step 1: trim Scene 1 + Scene 3 into separate clips.
  ffmpeg -ss 0 -t 5 -i refactored/data/media/viral_videos/eagle_on_wooden_bridge.mp4 -c copy /tmp/eagle-part1.mp4
  ffmpeg -ss 12 -t 7 -i refactored/data/media/viral_videos/eagle_on_wooden_bridge.mp4 -c copy /tmp/eagle-part2.mp4
Step 2: concat with concat demuxer (no re-encode = fast, no quality loss).
  printf 'file /tmp/eagle-part1.mp4\nfile /tmp/eagle-part2.mp4\n' > /tmp/eagle-filelist.txt
  ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i /tmp/eagle-filelist.txt -c copy /tmp/eagle-cut-12s.mp4
  ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration /tmp/eagle-cut-12s.mp4  # should print ~12.0
Step 3: upload /tmp/eagle-cut-12s.mp4 to Google Drive (yields new drive_file_id 'XYZ').
Step 4: update THIS manifest's drive_file_id field from 1UIcLfmGpf5kQZ4zD9nYy5xisQQss7liP to 'XYZ' and lower duration_fallback_seconds from 19 to 12; rerun:
  ./scripts/batch_index_drive_clips.sh --apply --pattern 'eagle*.json' --build
Step 5: rerun the batch wrapper with the new manifest. The asset gets a fresh asset.id == 'XYZ' with duration ~12s measured by ffprobe.
metadata.alternative_cut_options:
OPTION strict_takeoff_only: drop Scene 1 + 2, keep only Scene 3 (8s) = just takeoff shot. Use if Scene 1 setup is also deemed inutile. ffmpeg: ffmpeg -ss 12 -t 7 -i <parent>.mp4 -c copy /tmp/eagle-cut-8s-takeoff.mp4
OPTION trim_opening_then_drop_static: drop Scene 2 + opening 1s of Scene 1, keep tail of Scene 1 (1s..5s = 4 seconds of action only) + Scene 3 (12s..19s = 7 seconds). Result = 4s + 7s = 11s. ffmpeg: ffmpeg -ss 1 -t 4 -i <parent>.mp4 -c copy /tmp/eagle-part1-trimmed.mp4 && ffmpeg -ss 12 -t 7 -i <parent>.mp4 -c copy /tmp/eagle-part2.mp4 && concat.
OPTION keep_full_19s: NO cut, all 3 scenes. Use if user changed their mind and wants the full unedited asset. ffmpeg: cp <parent>.mp4 /tmp/eagle-cut-full-19s.mp4
